title: introduce-temporal-attested-rbac-grants-and-audit-blinding-shim
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: provide a safer pattern for short-lived elevated operator grants by introducing temporally-bound RBAC v2 grants that are cryptographically attested and paired with an audit blinding shim. This addresses live-operator attack windows, noisy audit channels for sensitive escalation events, and the need for KMS-backed proof of intent for compliance reviews. Summary of changes: 1) RBAC runtime: add temporalGrant API and evaluator that supports start/expiry, one-time-use tokens, and constraint expressions (namespace, service, action). Grants are persisted to the policy store with an HMAC and a KMS-wrapped signature for non-repudiation. 2) Attestation flow: operator requests a grant via existing operator API; a new attestation service performs policy checks, issues a short-lived attestation token signed with KMS CMK, and stores a compact proof in the attest-store. 3) Audit blinding shim: conditional blinding layer on the audit pipeline that replaces sensitive fields with reversible tokens and writes a blinded copy to the public audit stream; a separate sealed-audit vault holds the reversible mapping encrypted with the customer's CMK. 4) Compliance hooks: add an admin-only replay endpoint that rehydrates blinded audits after authorization and verifies attestation signatures before returning plaintext. 5) Migration and compatibility: new temporal grants are optional behind the feature flag security.temporal_attested_rbac. Old static grants continue to work; the evaluator performs precedence checks so temporal grants can be scoped more narrowly. Checklist: - [x] design doc (Linear ENG-4521) linked - [x] unit tests for evaluator and attestation signer - [x] e2e flow test for operator request -> attestation -> audited event - [x] KMS integration tests with test CMK - [x] basic load test to validate attestation service under 500 rps - [x] docs and console UI hint copy Draft rollout plan: enable feature flag off by default; deploy attestation service and evaluator in canary mode to a subset of control-plane nodes; on success, enable for orgs in pilot; after 2 weeks, global rollout. Security review: design reviewed by SecEng (SEC-213) and approved with minor hardening suggestions applied. Migration notes: no automated changes to existing RBAC policies; admins can opt-in by creating temporal grants via console or API. Observability: new metrics rbac.temporal_grants.requested, rbac.temporal_grants.issued, attest.sign_failures, audit.blindings.emitted added to control-plane telemetry; new audit tag "attestation_id" is included in blinded and sealed records. Risks and mitigations: - Risk: misuse of blinding could hide malicious activity. Mitigation: sealed-audit vault access requires CMK unwrap and admin rehydration flow with multi-party approval (two approvers). - Risk: KMS latency impacts attestation path. Mitigation: local caching of attestation proofs with short TTL and fallback signed HMAC when KMS unavailable (telemetry flagged). Rollback: remove feature flag and expire issued temporal grants; attestation tokens remain verifiable but enforcement disabled. Full description and design are in Linear ENG-4521 and design doc attached to the PR.

review_comments: Evan Brooks: Overall this looks solid; please add a fast-path for KMS-unavailable mode and measure effect on median latencies.
Maya Chen: Added local proof cache with 1m TTL and documented the failure mode; results from load test included in CI artifacts.
Sanjay Rao: Audit blinding is powerful but dangerous — we need a strict RBAC check around rehydration endpoint and HSM audit of access. Please add guardrails.
Maya Chen: Rehydration endpoint now requires two admin approvals and logs a non-blindable event to the sealed-vault access log; added e2e asserting approval flow.
Priya Nair: Integration tests show intermittent flakiness with test CMK in the CI matrix; suggest an integration-only retry wrapper.
Maya Chen: Added retry wrapper with jitter to integration KMS calls and a test-only deterministic stub in CI to stabilize builds.
ci_checks: load-test: pass (attestation service sustained 600 rps during CI run)
release_notes: Introduces opt-in temporal RBAC grants with cryptographic attestation and a reversible audit blinding shim. Admins can use temporal grants for short-lived operator elevation; blinded audit streams protect sensitive fields while sealed audit vaults retain rehydration capability under strict approval. Feature gated behind security.temporal_attested_rbac.
